# FCS Feature Usage Overview

The FCS standards have many features which are likely not evenly used across
vendors and software. This attempts to enumerate some common (and less common)
features.

## Keyword usage

These are optional keywords in all versions in which they are valid.

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_kw_usage"]])`">

## Scaling type

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_scaling"]])`">

## CRC usage

This checks for files that have a non-zero CRC word at the end.

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_crc"]])`">

## Datasets per file

Most files will have only one dataset in them (ie a discrete FCS data unit
defined by *\$NEXTDATA*)

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_datasets"]])`">

## *DATA* schema usage

These are different methods (schema) used to encode the bytes of data in *DATA*.

Note that "uint-var" is only possible in 3.1 and 3.2, and "mixed" is only
possible in 3.2.

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_schema"]])`">

## *\$BYTEORD* usage

Checks for either big endian, little endian, or something else (ie the PDP-11
layout which is 3,4,1,2)

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_byteord"]])`">

## *ANALYSIS* segment usage

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_analysis"]])`">

## *OTHER* segment usage

These are segments that can be used for anything. Most files have zero.

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_other_seg"]])`">

## Supplemental *TEXT* segment usage

Presumably this is only needed if *TEXT* gets so big that its ending offset
exceeds 100,000,000 and thus won't fit in *HEADER*.

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_supp_text"]])`">

## Dark segment usage

This isn't really a "feature" as much a loophole. Some files have extra data
that isn't indexed by any segment offsets. In that sense these are "dark" since
they can't be seen in a standards-compliant manner. However, they are still
there and probably mean something to someone, somewhere. These are called "dark
bytes" or "dark segments" (like "dark matter").

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_dark"]])`">

# FCS Standard Compliance Errors

This is an overview of all the errors that `fireflow` caught when parsing these
files. These are described in some detail below. Note that in many cases these
are aggregate errors in the sense that they indicate "at least one keyword" (or
similar) had an error. 

Each error on the x axis of the following plot is explained below.

### Offset errors

These are errors pertaining to offsets, ie the three offset pairs for *TEXT*,
*DATA*, and *ANALYSIS* in the *HEADER* and the *\$BEGIN/END* offsets in *TEXT*.
This also covers errors with *\$NEXTDATA* which is also an offset.

1) nc_offsets_analysis: *ANALYSIS* offsets either could not be parsed or the
   *HEADER* and *TEXT* offsets mismatched
2) nc_offsets_data: analogous to (1) for *DATA*
3) nc_offsets_data_len: *DATA* was not evenly divisible by the event width and
   was truncated to make this true.
4) nc_offsets_nextdata: *$NEXTDATA* does not actually point to the next dataset
   if it is non-zero.
5) nc_offsets_overflow_last: Final segment offset in the file exceeded the end
   of the file
6) nc_offsets_pseudoempty: At least one offset pair was empty but was written as
   `0,-1` or similar.
7) nc_offsets_supp: The supplemental *TEXT* offsets were either unparsable or
   duplicated another segment offset pair exactly.

### TEXT layout errors

These are errors pertaining to the *TEXT* segment byte layout.

Note that supplemental *TEXT* is included when evaluating these errors if it
exists. For almost all files this is not relevant.

1) nc_text_byte_pair: A key or value had an invalid byte sequence. For keys,
   means a non-ASCII byte was encountered. For values this means a non-UTF8 byte
   was encountered.
2) nc_text_delim_number: The *TEXT* segment had an even number of delimiters.
   Note that every value *TEXT* segment (regardless of escaping) must have an
   odd delimiter number.
3) nc_text_delimiter: The delimiter was not a byte from 1 to 126.
4) nc_text_non_escape: The delimiter needed to be escaped for *TEXT* to be
   parsed validly.
5) nc_text_nonstd_nonunique: A given non-stdandard key (no prepended "$") was
   encountered at least twice.
6) nc_text_std_nonunique: A given stdandard key (prepended "$") was encountered
   at least twice.
7) nc_text_token_blank_key: A blank key was encountered.
8) nc_text_token_blank_value: A blank value was encountered. This is only
   possible for escaped *TEXT* segments.
9) nc_text_token_boundary: An escaped delimiter pair was encountered next to
   a real delimiter. This is an error because it is ambiguous.
10) nc_text_token_number: The number of tokens was even. All valid *TEXT*
    must have an even number of tokens since these need to be grouped as
    key/value pairs.
11) nc_text_token_trimmed: A value which was entirely whitespace was trimmed to
    a blank value. This is only possible for unescaped *TEXT* segments.
12) nc_text_utf8: *TEXT* had invalid UTF-8 bytes. `fireflow` in these cases
    interprets *TEXT* as Latin-1 (aka ISO-8859-1).

### Keyword value standardization errors

These errors pertain to standardization of the keyword values into a
higher-level data schema specific to each FCS version.

They can be roughly grouped into general and specialized parsing errors:

#### General

1) nc_key_val_optional: At least one optional keyword could not be parsed and
   was dropped.
2) nc_key_val_scale_forced: At least one *\$PnE* keyword encoded a non-linear
   scale for a measurement that required a linear scale (either the time
   measurement or a floating-point measurement).
3) nc_key_val_scale_log: At least one *\$PnE* keyword had an invalid log scale
   value (something like `1,0`)
4) nc_key_val_timestep_invalid: *\$TIMESTEP* could not be parsed and was required.
5) nc_key_val_timestep_missing: *\$TIMESTEP* was missing and was required.
6) nc_key_val_ws_edge: At least one value had whitespace on either the left or
   right that was trimmed off to enable valid parsing of the value (usually a
   number)
7) nc_key_val_ws_inner: At least one sub-value in a comma-separated keyword
   value had whitespace between the value and the comma that needed to be
   trimmed to enable a valid parse.
8) nc_key_val_pnn_non_unique: At least one pair of *\$PnN* values were not
   unique.

#### Specialized

1) nc_parse_begindatetime_fmt: The format for *\$BEGINDATETIME* was invalid.
2) nc_parse_enddatetime_fmt: Same as (1) for *\$ENDDATETIME*.
3) nc_parse_btim_fmt: Same as (1) for *\$BTIM*.
4) nc_parse_etim_fmt: Same as (1) for *\$ETIM*.
5) nc_parse_date_fmt: Same as (1) for *\$DATE*.
6) nc_parse_last_modified_fmt: Same as (1) for *\$LAST_MODIFIED*.
7) nc_parse_spillover_names: The names for *\$SPILLOVER* were actually numbers
   which should be properly interpreted as measurement indices.
   
### Extra keyword errors

These are errors pertaining to keywords that look like standardized keywords (ie
they have a "$" in the front) yet are not really part of the FCS standard for
the file.

Note, this has a relationship to the `nc_version` error in the next section
because it depends on which FCS version the file is assumed to follow based on
a heuristic that guesses the version given the keywords present. For a full
description of this, see the `fireflow` documentation (specifically the
`version_override` flag).

For purposes here, the version is changed from that indicated in *HEADER* if a
different version can be selected that drops no keywords (optional or required).
If impossible, the version which drops the least optional keywords is selected.

1) nc_extra_hyper_gate: At least one *\$Gm* keyword has an index which exceeds
   *\$GATE*.
2) nc_extra_hyper_par: At least one *\$Pn* keyword has an index which exceeds
   *\$PAR*.
3) nc_extra_other_version: At least one keywords was found which belongs to
   another version but is invalid in this file's selected version.
4) nc_extra_pseudostd: At least one keyword was found which starts with "$" but
   does not belong any FCS standard version.
5) nc_extra_temporal_optical: At least one keyword in the time measurement was
   found which should only be present on an optical measurement (ie *\$PnL*,
   *\$PnG*, etc).
   
### Misc errors

1) nc_bitmask: At least one measurement had an integer value which exceeded the
   *$PnR* bitmask.
2) nc_byteord: *$BYTEORD* did not reflect the actual layout of data in the 
   *DATA* segment. This only applies to integer layouts for FCS 2.0/3.0.
3) nc_crc_validity: The CRC existed and matched the computed CRC of the file.
4) nc_crc_word: The 8-byte CRC word was found immediately after the last segment
   of the file. It may be all zero. No attempt is made to find CRCs after 
   "other stuff" in the FCS file that are not indexed as segments (although 
   these exist in many cases). This does not apply to FCS 2.0 since CRC was
   introduced in FCS 3.0.
5) nc_int_width: The width of *\$PnB* did not match the actual width of the data
   in *DATA* and/or the *\$BYTEORD* keywords. This only applies to integer
   datatypes for FCS 2.0/3.0.
6) nc_tot: *\$TOT* did not match the actualy number of events in *DATA* (as
   computed using the sum of *\$PnB* and the length of the *DATA* segment in
   bytes.
7) nc_version: The version in *HEADER* did not match the "real" version of the
   file. "Real" version is defined here as the version which drops the least
   number of optional keywords. If the *HEADER* version is tied on this metric
   with a different version, the former is chosen.

<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(snakemake@input[["plot_errors"]])`">
